asks: Nothing in the glossary creates a Project or a Task. Should creation be spec'd, or is it deliberately outside the vocabulary?
because: The glossary defines completeTask, reopenTask and deleteProject — every state transition except the first one. Implementing the app meant inventing createProject and createTask outright (app/src/domain/world.ts marks them as not spec-derived), which puts the most-used behaviour in the system outside the shared vocabulary.

options.label: Spec them
options.detail: Creation becomes part of the vocabulary, like every other transition. Note this forces a second decision: whether creating a RecurringTask is its own function or a variant of createTask — the ops below take the second reading.

ops.spec: Creates a Project with the given name. The new Project holds no Tasks. The name is not required to be unique — two Projects may share a name and remain distinct.
Creates a Task inside the given Project. The new Task is not done. Supplying a recurrenceRule creates a RecurringTask instead of a plain Task; omitting it creates a plain Task.

tests: a newly created Project holds no Tasks
a newly created Task is not done
creating two Projects with the same name yields two distinct Projects
createTask with a recurrenceRule yields a RecurringTask; without one it yields a plain Task

options.label: Leave creation out
options.detail: The glossary describes what can happen to things that already exist, and construction stays an implementation concern. Cheaper, but it means the app's most common operation has no shared name — you and the agent cannot refer to 'createTask' and mean the same thing, which is the failure this project exists to prevent.
